name: Bearfolk
body:
Often mistaken for werebears, these ursine humanoids are most common in the deep woods of the north. However, smaller communities of bearfolk have been spotted in many other areas around the world.

Physical

Bearfolk have features reminiscent of brown bears, but walk with an upright, bipedal posture and have fully articulated, quite nimble hands. Unlike some animalistic humanoids, bearfolk always wear clothing, usually mimicking the local human styles.

Social

Bearfolk are decent hunters, trappers, and craftspeople, and trade with dwarves, humans, and other nearby humanoids for weapons and other necessities they do not manufacture themselves.

Most bearfolk are shy but not timid. While they prefer to keep to themselves, they will fiercely defend their families and villages.

They readily tap into their savage ursine instincts in battle, rearing up to show tooth and claw and intimidate their foes into cowering before them.

Alignment and Religion

Bearfolk are most commonly Chaotic Neutral, as their primary motivations are autonomy and self-determination. Most are solitary creatures who prefer to be left alone, forming loosely connected, isolated communities only for the sake of and trade and mutual defense. While some bearfolk, especially druids, embrace Neutrality, few lean Lawful. An equal number tend toward Good or Evil.

The druidic faith is appealing to many bearfolk, who have a deep appreciation for nature. However, just as many eschew faith altogether, or embrace elements of religion borrowed from a local humanoid culture.

Names

Some typical bearfolk names include the following (choose or roll 1d12):

Bert
Bev
Danick
Darce
Feelik
Gord
Jozee
Linden
Louee
Melle
Ozer
Sofee
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are powerful and intuitive, but not adept at higher education. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Wis, –2 Int [standard]. (0)
Size Medium. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type Humanoid. You are a Humanoid with the bearfolk subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Dwarven, Elven, Gnome, Giant, and Sylvan. (0)
Other Traits
Claws You have two claw attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d4 damage each. (2)
Intimidating You receive a +2 species bonus on Intimidate checks due to your fearsome nature. (2)
Senses Low-light vision. You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Natural Armor You have a tough, resilient hide that provides a +1 natural armor bonus. (2)
Outdoor Skills Climb and Survival are always class skills for you. (1)
Special Senses Scent. You have the scent universal monster ability. (4)
Total: 12 RP (Advanced)
Alternate Traits
Bearfolk Psionics You gain Wild Talent as a bonus feat at 1st level. If you take levels in a psionic class, you instead gain the Psionic Talent feat. When you take a level in a favored class, you can choose to gain an additional power point instead of a hit point or skill point. Finally, once per day, you can use thicken skin as a psi-like ability, using your character level as your manifester level. This trait replaces scent.
Bite Unlike many bearfolk, you have not worked to honed your claws to razor sharpness, but your oversized canines instead. You have a bite attack; this is a primary natural attack that deals 1d4 damage. This trait replaces claws.
Cold Protection You gain cold resistance 5 and are unaffected by environmental cold. This trait replaces natural armor.
Cultured You are used to being around other humanoids, and are more outgoing and worldly than most bearfolk, but less coordinated physically. You gain +2 Str, +2 Cha, –2 Dex. In addition, you gain a +2 species bonus to Knowledge (local) checks. This trait alters ability score modifiers and replaces intimidating.
Burst of Ferocity Once per day, when you are brought below 0 hit points but not killed, you can fight on for 1 more round as if disabled. At the end of your next turn, unless brought to above 0 hit points, you immediately fall unconscious and begin dying. This trait replaces intimidating.
Keen Senses You receive a +2 species bonus on Perception checks. This trait replaces intimidating.
Master Hunter You receive a +2 species bonus on Stealth checks. This trait replaces intimidating.
Sea Skills You are adept at surviving along the coast or out at sea. Knowledge (geography) and Swim are always class skills for you. This trait replaces outdoor skills.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add +1 to your total number of rage rounds per day.
Bard Add +1 to your total number of bardic performance rounds per day.
Bloodrager Add +1 to your total number of bloodrage rounds per day.
Cleric Select one domain power granted at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Wisdom modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that domain power.
Druid Add +1/3 to your natural armor bonus when using wild shape.
Fighter Add a +2 bonus on rolls to stabilize when dying.
Oracle Add +1/6 to your effective oracle level for the purpose of determining the effects of one revelation.
Psychic Warrior Add +1/2 to concentration checks when manifesting psychic warrior powers.
Ranger Add +1/4 to a single existing favored terrain bonus (maximum bonus +1 per favored terrain). You must be at least 3rd level to select this benefit.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Disable Device checks in wilderness settings and a +1/2 bonus to trap sense when you’re in the wilderness.
Skald Add +1 to your total number of raging song rounds per day.
Sorcerer Select one bloodline power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that bloodline power.
Spirit Warrior Add +1 to your total number of rounds per day that you can use your aura ability.
Witch Add +1/4 natural armor bonus to the AC of your familiar.
